answers: One good example is a Plinko-style museum installation Dave built with Three.js and Rapier. The user only saw one ball drop, but behind the scenes the simulation may have run thousands of times to find a physically valid path that matched their dial settings and launch timing.

Dave led a non-deterministic Plinko-style museum installation with the VXD team. It used Three.js and Rapier, physical dials, a sweeping launcher, and fast-forwarded physics simulations to find a valid ball path before showing the visitor one clean drop.

The Plinko project is a strong Dave story: real physics, physical controls, a big portrait display, and a simulation that could run thousands of invisible attempts so the one visible drop satisfied the right bucket and collision sequence.
